body.statement: For some \(c_\alpha>0\) depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class constants, every uniformly honest interval obeys \[\liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{C_N\in\mathfrak C_{N,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_N(u)}\frac{E_P[\ell(C_N)]}{\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}}\ge c_\alpha\] for every admissible \(u=u_N>0\) with nonempty \(\mathcal M_N(u)\). The split-support continuum has \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}=1/(4n)\), \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}=4n\mu_n^2\), and bounded divergence at CACE displacement \(h\asymp\min\{1,T_{\mathrm{coll}}^{-1/2}\}\). Cellwise dual compensated tilts extend the construction to every allocation face and yield Kullback--Leibler geometry dual to \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}\).
body.justification: The result covers all confidence procedures and makes the collection quadratic program necessary.
body.gap: Cai and Low give general testing machinery, but no published lower family preserves encouragement randomization, exclusion, monotonicity, transport, and union support while inducing this program.
body.consumer: The theorem rules out pooled and single-source procedures that claim uniform gains over collection profiling.
body.proof_tex:
For every feasible allocation, Cauchy--Schwarz and residual regularity give
\[
 W_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T,a)
 \ge v_0\sum_{s,x}\frac{a_{sx}^2}{n_sp_s(x)}
 \ge\frac{v_0(\sum_{s,x}a_{sx})^2}{\sum_{s,x}n_sp_s(x)}
 =\frac{v_0}{N}.
\]
Since \(0<\mu_D\le1\), nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_N(u)\) entails \(u\le N/v_0\).

Now use a support-split continuum. The displayed split family has
\(V_{\mathrm{coll}}=1/(4n)\) and \(T_{\mathrm{coll}}=4n\mu_n^2\). More generally, changing its bounded Rademacher amplitude and, if needed, choosing a propensity in \([e_0,1-e_0]\), gives a price \(q\) down to the class floor. The same calculation gives
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}=\frac qN,\qquad
 T_{\mathrm{coll}}=\frac{N\mu^2}{q}.
\]
Choose \(q\) and \(\mu\in(0,1]\) so that the latter strength is at least \(u\). The bounded-outcome variance ceiling and the preceding necessary inequality ensure this for every nonempty strength class. Set
\[
 h=c\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\},
\]
where \(c>0\) depends only on the fixed class constants and is small enough that all Bernoulli tilts remain in their simplices. The compensated split construction, with a variance-preserving second-order adjustment if a residual-price constraint is active, gives \(P_0,P_h\in\mathcal M_N\) such that
\[
 \theta_T(P_0)=0,\qquad\theta_T(P_h)=h,\qquad
 P_0\in\mathcal M_N(u),\qquad
 \operatorname{KL}(P_h,P_0)\le C N\mu^2h^2/q\le Cc^2.
\]
The final inequality uses \(N\mu^2/q\asymp u\) and \(uh^2\le c^2\). Taking \(c\) smaller makes total variation at most
\(\eta_\alpha<(1-2\alpha)/2\). To verify this without an undeclared testing premise, apply
\[
 t\log t-t+1\ge\frac{(t-1)^2}{2(t+1)}
\]
to the likelihood ratio and then Cauchy--Schwarz; this gives
\(\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_h,P_0)/2}\).

Let \(C_N\) be uniformly honest. Its coverage at both laws is \(1-\alpha-o(1)\). Changing measure for the second coverage event and using the union bound yields
\[
 P_0\{0\in C_N,\ h\in C_N\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1)-\|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
On this event an interval has length at least \(|h|\). Therefore, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 E_{P_0}\ell(C_N)
 \ge |h|\{1-2\alpha-o(1)-\eta_\alpha\}
 \ge c_\alpha\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\mathcal M_N(u)\), the infimum over honest procedures, and the lower limit proves the bound.

For a general support face, the information-modulus calculation gives quadratic cost \(\sum_xI_xb_x^2\). Minimization under \(\sum_xp_T(x)b_x=-\mu_Dh\) gives \(h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}\). Thus the split witness supplies the rate lower bound, and the dual cellwise tilts show that the necessity geometry on every face is exactly the collection quadratic program rather than a pooled scalar surrogate.
